title: Qualify multi-UID permissions and compatibility on Linux
description: Implement PRD acceptance gates 1-9 in a disposable provisioned Linux environment using three real UIDs and multiple clients. Include method coverage, raw-wire sentinels, guessed IDs, race/lifecycle failures, socket paths, performance and old-client rejection. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Repeatable suite fails against missing authorisation/projection; approved disposable account provisioning only; role matrix and failure injection pass; private sessions retain behaviour; applicable just check/CI and frozen contracts pass; 1/15-pane and multi-client results recorded.

title: Document sharing setup, privileges, recovery and fork maintenance
description: Publish unreleased user/operator documentation under docs/next, including group setup, attach commands, owner UI, account deprovisioning and UID reuse limits, revocation, private endpoints, remote restrictions, corrupt-policy recovery and explicit trusted-controller scope. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Fresh Linux operator follows documented setup; recovery never opens access by default; Control warning matches actual process privileges; implementation coverage and deferred isolation are stated; source rebase/merge compatibility checks documented; no published release snapshots edited.

title: Add bounded owner-only shared-access audit records
description: Implement R7 logs for attach/detach, policy revisions, grant/revoke, sharing state and denied actions. Record principal, object scope, operation and outcome without terminal content or credentials. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Logs are owner-only, bounded and rate-limited; relevant policy changes correlate by revision; participant responses contain no private audit detail; burst denial test cannot exhaust storage or block terminal service.

title: Build the owner Space access administration screen
description: Implement R3 using existing mouse-first modal/settings UI. Show selected OS user, space permission matrix, connected clients, stale grants, save/cancel/revoke and disable sharing. Default to View and require explicit acknowledgement for Control execution privileges. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Owner can assign/revoke permissions end-to-end; cancel has no effects; acknowledgement names terminal execution user; non-owners cannot invoke screen; empty state reveals no private metadata; keyboard and mouse paths share policy-backed actions.

title: Expose owner-only user lookup and grant management API
description: Implement R3 administration methods, optional negotiated capabilities, OS-user search including NSS lookup without enumeration, grant listing and atomic revision-checked save. Global user lists and stale grant details stay owner-only. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Non-owner direct API calls fail; service accounts hidden by default but explicit resolvable users supported; concurrent saves conflict safely; UID/name mismatches displayed; policy acknowledged only after durable save; frozen endpoint codecs unchanged.

title: Apply revocation atomically across streams and session lifecycle
description: Implement R6 revision invalidation, queue barriers, controller release, stream/wait cancellation, cached surface cleanup and unsupported-client disconnect. Cover deletion/moves, account refresh, sharing disable, restart, corruption, restore and handoff. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Barrier-based race tests prove no new post-revoke input/output is admitted under old policy; View downgrade releases control; old grants do not resurrect; unsupported shared handoff refuses; already-delivered bytes are accurately documented as unrecoverable.

title: Filter snapshots, events, terminal output and transferred assets
description: Implement R5 recipient-specific projections across metadata, focus fallback, aggregate counts, badges, notifications, event subscriptions, retained rendering, process details, file/graphics payloads and reconnect. Preserve pure shared state and hot-path performance. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Forbidden sentinel IDs/names/cwd/output are absent in raw payloads for unauthorised clients; View output works without input ownership or remote resize; no-access state creates no workspace; event opening and delivery both check permission; 1/15-pane projection costs measured.

title: Add explicit group-scoped sharing and cross-account attachment
description: Implement R2 with a separate owner-controlled group-connectable endpoint, owner verification, explicit owner/session targeting and safe discovery. Keep existing private endpoints and home/state permissions intact. Users SSH in as themselves; unsupported native remote bridges refuse safely. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Owner/Alice/Bob can attach using real accounts with expected denials; non-members cannot connect; group members without grants see empty state; socket/directory modes and symlink/stale-path tests pass; disable sharing preserves panes; no sudo or root daemon introduced.

title: Enforce policy across API, TUI and direct terminal commands
description: Implement R4 using one central evaluator and authoritative current object-to-workspace resolution at execution time. Cover schema methods, aliases/current targets, owner-only global actions, agent operations, keyboard/mouse, resize, takeover, popups, clipboard and batches. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Inventory-driven tests cover every ingress; unknown new methods deny; View has no shared mutations; Control cannot cross workspace or call global admin actions; inaccessible and unknown IDs have equivalent errors; queued actions recheck permissions.

title: Persist workspace grants and implement pure authorisation rules
description: Implement R1, R4 and R6 policy model: owner effective UID, host binding, UID/name principals, stable workspace IDs, None/View/Control, schema/revision and atomic owner-only persistence. Define classification for global and unscoped objects. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Role/action matrix has deterministic unit coverage; unknown operations deny; corrupt shared policy fails closed; owner cannot be revoked; username mismatch suspends grants; new/recreated workspaces have no grants; state file modes verified.

title: Bind kernel OS principals to every connection
description: Implement R1 in platform abstraction and client/API acceptance. Carry immutable UID/GID/PID where available through synchronous and queued requests. Resolve NSS display names outside render paths; fail closed when credentials cannot be verified. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Real multi-UID processes authenticate correctly; payload UID/name spoofing has no effect; failed peer lookup denies; identity persists through endpoint commands, waits and subscriptions; other platforms retain private-mode compilation.

title: Confirm shared-access threat model and inventory every transport
description: Review the pinned source and PRD. Classify each API method, TUI command, legacy input, terminal stream, event, file/graphics transfer, restore and remote bridge. Record selected endpoint layout and capability contract. Confirm trusted-controller phase one and isolate stronger claims behind phase two. Specification: .local/prd/os-user-space-access.md
acceptance_criteria: Checked-in method/transport inventory has default-deny classifications; architecture decision names execution identity, owner bypass boundary, account-refresh bound, revocation ordering and compatibility strategy; no unexamined transport remains.

title: OS-user permissions for shared Herdr spaces
description: Deliver Linux shared sessions where the owner assigns verified OS users View or Control access per workspace. Follow PRD R1-R7. Initial controllers are explicitly trusted with the terminal execution account; do not claim filesystem isolation.
acceptance_criteria: All phase-one children pass their acceptance gates; multi-UID end-to-end qualification passes; private-mode compatibility retained; owner admin screen and documentation shipped.

title: Publish OS-user space access PRD and implementation backlog
description: Prepare the requested EchBTI fork planning deliverables, verify source boundaries, create dependency-linked implementation beads, and publish recoverable planning data to the fork.
acceptance_criteria: PRD and Beads backlog published to EchBTI/herdr; dependencies validated; no runtime implementation claimed.
close_reason: Fork and source-backed PRD prepared; dependency-linked implementation backlog created and checked. Publication verified at session handoff.

title: Prove isolated execution resists cross-space and owner-account escape
description: Qualify phase-two execution with adversarial commands, spawned agents, socket discovery, symlinks, environment inspection, /proc access where relevant, credential access, network paths and worker restart/revocation. Update product claims only after evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Cross-space and owner-socket attempts fail in supported configuration; read/write and process escape suite passes; residual risks and provisioning constraints documented; explicit release review authorises stronger separation claims.

title: Implement isolated workers, scoped integration credentials and migration
description: Execute the approved phase-two worker design. Keep authenticated human identity distinct from worker UID. Agents receive workspace-scoped reporting/control credentials; never hand them owner sockets or owner environment. Implement provisioning checks, per-space mounts, crash recovery and opt-in migration.
acceptance_criteria: Unprivileged daemon can manage provisioned workers without arbitrary elevation; cross-space mounts and owner credentials absent; scoped tokens resist forgery/replay across spaces; execution identity shown correctly; crashes and migration preserve fail-closed boundaries.

title: Choose and validate an isolated worker and scoped-broker architecture
description:
## Rationale
OS-user authentication does not isolate owner-run shells. Select an execution boundary before promising confidentiality between controllers. Follow the PRD phase-two scope.

## Alternatives Considered
Separate worker OS accounts with a constrained broker; containers with restricted mounts and credentials. Compare privilege/provisioning needs, /proc and network exposure, crash recovery, migration, and maintenance.

## Decision Required
Record the selected worker architecture, explicit host provisioning, service identities, per-space mounts, network/secret policy and proof-of-boundary tests before implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture decision names worker privileges, broker capabilities and residual host-admin trust; executable escape-test plan covers owner sockets, host files and cross-space credentials; implementation may start only after decision is resolved.

title: Isolate shared-space execution from the session owner
description: Phase two: support controllers who must not inherit owner-account authority or access other projects. Design restricted worker accounts/containers, filesystem and credential boundaries and a scoped broker. Main daemon remains unprivileged. This is separate from phase-one Herdr visibility ACLs.
acceptance_criteria: Selected worker architecture and threat model approved; workspace process cannot reach owner sockets, other workspace files/credentials, host namespaces or unscoped control APIs; escape tests and migration/recovery pass before confidential-isolation claims.
